issues.legal_issue: A public authority’s status does not justify condoning an unexplained and negligently incurred delay in filing a revision challenging the rejection of an execution objection.
material_facts: A decree declaring title and granting a permanent injunction was passed against the State and was affirmed on appeal, after which it became final.
The State’s first objection to execution was dismissed, but the State did not promptly challenge that order.
The State later filed a further execution objection, which was rejected, and sought revision of the earlier rejection only after attachment proceedings had begun.
The State’s application to condone the delay did not show sufficient cause for the delay.
issues.conclusion: The delay in filing the revision should not have been condoned; the appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the application to condone delay was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, sufficient cause is assessed pragmatically and in a justice-oriented manner, but a liberal approach is not automatic, even for the State. The State must establish sufficient cause, and serious laches or negligence will not be excused merely because the applicant is the Government. Delay in seeking execution of a decree does not itself justify delay in challenging an order rejecting an execution objection. The Court relied on Union of India v. Nirpen Sharma, AIR 2011 SC 1237, concerning the Government’s delay in deciding whether to appeal.

rule.if: revision_seeking_condonation_of_delay and prior_execution_objection_dismissed and challenge_delayed_until_execution_steps_advanced and delay_not_supported_by_sufficient_cause

predicates.revision_seeking_condonation_of_delay: The applicant seeks condonation of delay in filing a revision challenging an order made in execution proceedings.
predicates.prior_execution_objection_dismissed: An earlier objection to execution was dismissed and the applicant did not promptly challenge that dismissal.
predicates.challenge_delayed_until_execution_steps_: The applicant waited until execution proceedings had advanced before challenging the earlier dismissal.
predicates.delay_not_supported_by_sufficient_cause: The applicant did not establish a sufficient cause explaining the delay.

issues.definition: When a delayed revision challenging the rejection of an execution objection is filed only after execution has advanced, and the applicant has not established sufficient cause for the delay, condonation is denied.
